language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi friends, my name is Ralph. I'm a fifth grader at the Antarctica Elementary School. I love science and learning how the world works.
Living in Antartica means I see many changes in the way the Southern Ocean behaves. What's interesting to see is how the Moon influences the tide and the changing sea levels.
You might be wondering how something so far away, like the Moon, can affect the tides here on earth.
Did you know that the Moon's gravitational force pulls the water of oceans and seas that surround us, causing a "swell" directly below the Moon and on the opposite side of the planet too.
This causes "high tides" and the oceans and seas on the other side experience "low tides."

Gravity or gravitational forces are forces of attraction. Every object in the universe that has mass exerts a gravitational pull or force on every other mass. The size of the pull depends on the mass of the object.
Can you help my class and I learn how the Moon influences the tide?
Let's get started!

Did you know that oceans and seas around the world experience high tides twice a day? The rest of the time they experience low tides.
Spring tides are another type of tides that occurs when the Moon is in line with the Earth and the Sun, causing added gravitational force from the Sun and even higher tides!
On the other hand, neap tides occur when the Moon and the Sun are at 90 degrees from each other, producing the lowest of the high tides.
There are two spring tides and two neap tides each month.
Phew, talk about complicating the situation. Can you help me?
